newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-COLLYMORE BACK HOME WITH ASTON VILLA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLLYMORE BACK HOME WITH ASTON VILLA.

text.p: England striker Stan Collymore always knew one day he would play for his hometown team -- Aston Villa.
He just never imagined he'd be wearing the famous claret and blue shirt for the first time in front of fewer than 9,000 fans in a meaningless friendly in Los Angeles.

More than 5,000 miles from Birmingham, and a week after Villa paid seven million pounds ($11.4 million) to Liverpool for him, Collymore scored on his debut last week in a 1-1 draw with the Los Angeles Galaxy of Major League Soccer.

His effortless header sparked nothing like the roar it would have brought from the Villa Park terraces, where a six-year-old Collymore first stood 20 years ago cheering a Villa team destined to become European champions in 1982.
In the Rose Bowl locker room after his debut, Collymore talked to Reuters about playing his first game for Villa.
"Emotional? Very, yes! It was a little bit strange because of the surroundings. I didn't expect to make my debut for Villa in the Rose Bowl in a game like this.

"But it will be more so back home with the premiership or the F.A. Cup at stake," he said of playing for a club with a rich tradition of seven league titles and seven F.A. Cup wins, as well as the European Cup.
He talked wistfully of the days he stood on the terraces.

"I was six years old. Twenty years ago, so it's come full circle," he said. "My sister and her husband took me a few times when I was younger. Then I started playing myself so I didn't have so much time. But I was pretty much a fan."
Collymore, a deadly striker himself, recalled the Villa goalscorers of the late 1970s and early 1980s, including Collymore's new manager Brian Little.
"When Villa won the European Cup in 81-82, the two guys who played up front were Peter Withe and Gary Shaw, so they were two of my idols.
"Players like (Michel) Platini in France, they were idols (too), but pretty much it was the Villa team of the early Eighties," he said.

The 26-year-old Collymore, who cost Liverpool a then British record of 8.5 million pounds ($13.8 million) when he moved from Nottingham Forest in June 1995, has signed a four-year contract with Villa, with a further one-year option.
His total transfer fees over the last four years total 17.7 million pounds ($28.7 million), so does the big price tag worry him?
"Not at all. You just go out and play, you're not conscious of it at all. You don't walk around the pitch thinking how much you cost, you're thinking to win games."
Collymore said he was happy to be joining his third big English premier league club.
"Very much so. I left a very big club in Liverpool and I've gone to another big club in Aston Villa, who've paid a lot of money," he said.
"I'll just concentrate on playing and hopefully win things and that's the main consideration. The financial thing is put to the side."
But after only two years at Anfield, where he sometimes struggled to make the team, does he have any regrets?

"My only regret really is that in the two years I was there we came close to winning. We lost the F.A. Cup to Manchester United, came third in the league the first season, reached the semifinal of the Cup Winners' Cup. Maybe the one regret is not winning anything in the time I was there, but I have some great memories of the place."
For now, Collymore's focused on winning with Villa, although he was reluctant to assess what strengths he can bring to a team flirting with honours for the last few seasons.
"That's for other people to decide. At Liverpool I think the strength was my pace, getting in behind players, creating and scoring goals.
"Hopefully if I can bring all those things to Villa it will be able to take them that little bit further than they have done the last couple of years."
A good season with them can only help his chances of winning more England caps too.
"I've had a couple of caps up till now, I want to add to that. If I have a good season, next season, with the World Cup coming up, I reckon I can sneak into the squad," he said.
But Aston Villa was Collymore's first love and the striker hopes it will be his last stop in football.
"I had two good years at Forest and two at Liverpool, so I'm looking to maybe seeing out the rest of my career at Villa. I hope so.
"It's an area where I was born and bred and that's very important to me to give something back."
